subject.title: [security] Remote git seed forwards password-bearing non-HTTP origin URLs to leases

question: Should Crabbox extend the existing git-seed credential guard to password-bearing non-HTTP URL-style remotes while keeping passwordless SSH remotes seedable?
rationale: The security boundary is clear, but the detector must distinguish password-bearing URL userinfo from ordinary SSH usernames without breaking established seedable SSH remotes.

options.title: Extend password-bearing URL detection
options.body: Treat non-HTTP URL userinfo with a password or token as credential-bearing, skip git seed with a redacted warning, and keep passwordless SSH forms seedable.

options.title: Block all URL userinfo
options.body: Treat any URL-style userinfo as unsafe, which is simpler but may break common ssh://git@host/repo.git workflows.

options.title: Defer for private seed credentials
options.body: Pause this fix until Crabbox has an explicit scoped private-repository seed credential mechanism that avoids argv and persisted remote config.

recommendation.title: Extend password-bearing URL detection
recommendation.body: Treat non-HTTP URL userinfo with a password or token as credential-bearing, skip git seed with a redacted warning, and keep passwordless SSH forms seedable.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle owns the merged HTTP(S) guard and most current history in the git-seed security boundary.
